newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees 150 bln DM turnover in 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees 150 bln DM turnover in 5 years.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG expected turnover to rise more than 50 percent to 150 billion marks over the next five years, chief financial officer Karl-Hermann Baumann told Reuters on Thursday.

Siemens also expected the sell-off of several business units this year to add extraordinary income for 1996/97, Baumann said. Siemens has forecast no improvement in profit for the current business year, which ends September 30.
"I would not rule out that business volume could go up to 150 billion marks in five years," Baumann said. Sales rose six percent to 94 billion marks in 1995/96.
Baumann repeated Siemens' forecast of no improvement over the 1995/96 net profit of 2.987 billion marks as well as the forecast of renewed profit growth in 1997/98 and 1998/99.
Profit this year would be dampened by falling prices of products such as semiconductors and medical systems.
Baumann also reiterated Siemens' profit goal of reaching a 15 percent yield on capital by the year 2000, and said serveral units were now operating below that level.

Siemens planned to sell of units with business volume totaling about 3.5 billion marks this year. The divestments would contribute extraordinary gains to Siemens' bottom line, although the total would be below the 496 million marks in extraordianary income booked last year.
